claims.text: What the image looks like Mobile echodensity (vegetation) on a valve, regurgitation, abscess → infective endocarditis
claims.quote: Mobile echodensity (vegetation) on valve, regurgitation, abscess Infective endocarditis

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Valves: morphology, regurg jets (color Doppler), gradient/area (CW Doppler)
claims.quote: Valves - morphology, regurg jets (color Doppler), gradient/area (CW Doppler).

claims.text: Duke imaging criterion: echo and/or cardiac CT showing vegetation, valvular/leaflet perforation/aneurysm, abscess, pseudoaneurysm or intracardiac fistula, or echo showing significant new valvular regurgitation (worsening or changing of preexisting regurgitation is not sufficient)
claims.quote: Echocardiography and/or cardiac CT showing vegetation, valvular/leaflet perforation/aneurysm, abscess, pseudoaneurysm, or intracardiac fistula OR Echocardiography showing significant new valvular regurgitation. Worsening or changing of preexisting regurgitation is not sufficient.

claims.text: TTE first (sensitivity 50 to 90%, specificity > 90%); TEE can reveal vegetations too small for TTE (sensitivity 90 to 100%)
claims.quote: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) should be done initially. It has sensitivity of 50 to 90% and specificity > 90% (3). Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) can reveal vegetations too small to be seen on TTE. It has sensitivity of 90 to 100% (4).

claims.text: TEE should be done with a prosthetic valve (TTE sensitivity is limited), when TTE is nondiagnostic, or when the diagnosis is established clinically (to detect perforations, abscesses and fistulas)
claims.quote: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) should be done when Patients have a prosthetic valve (where TTE sensitivity is limited) Transthoracic echocardiography is nondiagnostic Diagnosis of infective endocarditis has been established clinically (done to detect perforations, abscesses, and fistulas)

claims.text: Causes Infection of the endocardium, usually with bacteria (commonly streptococci or staphylococci) or fungi; vegetations may cause valvular incompetence or obstruction, myocardial abscess or mycotic aneurysm
claims.quote: Infective endocarditis is infection of the endocardium, usually with bacteria (commonly, streptococci or staphylococci) or fungi. It may cause fever, heart murmurs, petechiae, anemia, embolic phenomena, and endocardial vegetations. Vegetations may result in valvular incompetence or obstruction, myocardial abscess, or mycotic aneurysm.

claims.text: Predisposing: congenital heart defects, rheumatic valvular disease, bicuspid or calcific aortic valves, mitral valve prolapse, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, prior endocarditis and intracardiac devices
claims.quote: Predisposing cardiac abnormalities include congenital heart defects, rheumatic valvular disease, bicuspid or calcific aortic valves, mitral valve prolapse, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, prior endocarditis, and intracardiac devices.

claims.text: The nidus is usually a sterile fibrin-platelet vegetation formed when damaged endothelial cells release tissue factor
claims.quote: The nidus for infection is usually a sterile fibrin-platelet vegetation formed when damaged endothelial cells release tissue factor.

claims.text: Symptoms Subacute: initially vague: low-grade fever (< 39° C), night sweats, fatigability, malaise and weight loss; chills and arthralgias may occur; initially ≤ 15% have fever or a murmur, but eventually almost all develop both
claims.quote: Initially, symptoms of subacute bacterial endocarditis are vague: low-grade fever (< 39° C), night sweats, fatigability, malaise, and weight loss. Chills and arthralgias may occur. Symptoms and signs of valvular insufficiency may be a first clue. Initially, ≤ 15% of patients have fever or a murmur, but eventually almost all develop both.

claims.text: Acute and prosthetic valve endocarditis: similar but with a more rapid course; most frequent at presentation are fever (78%), murmur (65%) and congestive heart failure (27%)
claims.quote: Symptoms and signs of acute bacterial endocarditis and prosthetic valvular endocarditis are similar to those of subacute bacterial endocarditis, but the course is more rapid. Fever (78%), cardiac murmur (65%), and congestive heart failure (27%) are the most frequent symptoms at presentation (1).

claims.text: Roth spots (retinal hemorrhages with white centers), petechiae, Osler nodes (painful nodules on or near the tips of digits), Janeway lesions (nontender macules or papules on palms or soles) and splinter hemorrhages
claims.quote: Retinal emboli can cause round or oval hemorrhagic retinal lesions with small white centers (Roth spots). Cutaneous manifestations include petechiae (on the upper trunk, conjunctivae, mucous membranes, and distal extremities), painful erythematous subcutaneous nodules on or near the tips of digits (Osler nodes), nontender hemorrhagic macules or papules on the palms or soles (Janeway lesions), and splinter hemorrhages under the nails.

claims.text: Right-sided: septic pulmonary emboli may cause cough, pleuritic chest pain and sometimes hemoptysis; a tricuspid regurgitation murmur is typical
claims.quote: Septic pulmonary emboli may cause cough, pleuritic chest pain, and sometimes hemoptysis. A murmur of tricuspid regurgitation is typical.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: modified Duke criteria; IV antibiotics ± surgery
claims.quote: Modified Duke criteria; IV antibiotics ± surgery

claims.text: If suspected: at least 2 (ideally 3) sets of blood cultures under strict aseptic technique, one aerobic and one anaerobic culture in each set
claims.quote: If endocarditis is suspected, at least 2 (ideally 3) sets of blood cultures should be obtained under strict aseptic technique, with one aerobic and one anaerobic culture in each set.

claims.text: A prolonged course of antimicrobials, typically IV for 2 to 8 weeks; surgery may be needed for mechanical complications or resistant organisms
claims.quote: Treatment consists of a prolonged course of antimicrobial therapy (1). Surgery may be needed for mechanical complications or resistant organisms. Typically, antimicrobials are given IV. Because they must be given for 2 to 8 weeks, home IV therapy is often used.

claims.text: Surgery is typically indicated for heart failure, uncontrolled infection (eg, persistent infection, fungal or resistant organisms, heart block, abscess, aneurysm, fistula or enlarging vegetation) and embolic risk (eg, large vegetations > 10 mm or recurrent emboli)
claims.quote: Surgery is typically indicated in Patients with heart failure (particularly those with prosthetic, aortic, or native mitral valve endocarditis and those with pulmonary edema or cardiogenic shock) Patients with uncontrolled infection (those with persistent infection, infection with fungal or resistant organisms, recurrent prosthetic valve endocarditis, or endocarditis complicated by heart block, abscess, aneurysm, fistula, or enlarging vegetation) Patients at risk for embolism (particularly those with prosthetic, aortic, or native mitral valve endocarditis, and large vegetations [defined as > 10 mm] or those with recurrent emboli).
